cycles.method: Exact MKII package db843bc2 on RAM base 3a4c07fe. The longest observed guarded callback during the four matched 60-second playback runs took 16,820 ticks of the 132 MHz timer. The conditional bound for Grain's own zero-wait work is 157,940 core cycles for 16 source frames and 279,860 for 32. Stock calls, external-memory latency and interrupt interference have no proven upper bound. See TESTING.md, evidence/timing/side-first-comparison.json and evidence/timing/guard-trace.json.

load.method: Matched 60-second runs at 100 BPM on T5, the track with the longest candidate frame. The same 24-bit stereo R3 played under 20-channel USB capture and a musical MIDI phrase. Idle percent is 100 minus the median stock CPU meter reading during playback, excluding its first 3 seconds.

stress.droppedExplanation: Musical comparison on package db843bc2. Per run the host submitted 2,400 clocks, 200 note-ons, 200 note-offs and 50 modulation events over 60 seconds. The receive-error and transmit-drop counters are recorded separately from render skips and end-to-end MIDI delivery. Stuck notes and end-to-end message loss were not counted. UI and audio ticks advanced after STOP and Part changes. The earlier high-rate panel-freeze report is in TESTING.md.
